title: Dentist Salary Australia: National Minimum Wage vs Actual Earnings
description: Understand dentist salary Australia: the National Minimum Wage, award-free status, and how to convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax pay.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for a dentist in Australia?
faqs.a: Dentists working in private practice are not covered by any award, so the National Minimum Wage applies. From 1 July 2026, that is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per 38-hour week. Casual dentists receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, most dentists earn significantly more through negotiation or enterprise agreements.

Yes, if a dentist is employed as a casual and is award/agreement free, they are entitled to the 25% casual loading on top of the National Minimum Wage. This brings the casual rate to $33.05 per hour from 1 July 2026. The loading compensates for lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a dentist?

The super guarantee is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per quarter. Actual super will be higher if the dentist earns more.

bodyMarkdown:
## How the National Minimum Wage Applies to Dentists

According to the Fair Work Ombudsman, no award covers dentists working for private dental practices. This means they are award/agreement free employees and are entitled to the National Minimum Wage (NMW) and the National Employment Standards. The NMW from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission.

For casual dentists, a 25% loading applies, bringing the rate to $33.05 per hour. This loading is paid on top of the base rate and is intended to compensate for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements that permanent employees receive.

It is important to note that the NMW is the legal floor. Most dentists earn well above this minimum through negotiation, enterprise agreements, or because they are self-employed. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, which is a more realistic benchmark for a dentist salary Australia.

## What Dentists Actually Earn

While the NMW provides a baseline, dentist salaries in Australia vary widely based on experience, location, and whether the dentist is an employee or runs their own practice. The ABS figure of $2,083.70 per week for full-time employees gives an annual equivalent of approximately $108,352.40 (52 weeks). This is more than double the NMW annual amount of $52,274.72.

Many dentists are self-employed or work under practice agreements that set higher rates. Enterprise agreements may also apply, which can include penalty rates, allowances, and higher base pay. If you are negotiating a salary, it is wise to research the market and consider the value of your skills and experience.

## Converting Hourly to Annual, Fortnightly, and Weekly

To convert an hourly rate to annual gross pay, use the formula:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a dentist on the NMW working 38 hours per week:

- Annual: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,274.72
- Fortnightly: $26.44 × 38 × 2 = $2,009.44 (before tax and super)
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90

If you are paid a salary, you can reverse the calculation to find your hourly equivalent. For example, a salary of $108,352 per year (based on ABS average) divided by 52 weeks and 38 hours gives an hourly rate of about $54.84.

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool can help you quickly switch between hourly, weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures.

## Superannuation and Tax Considerations

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For a dentist earning the NMW, the employer must contribute an extra $6,272.97 per year (12% of $52,274.72). The super guarantee is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year, so for high earners the percentage applies only up to that limit.

Tax for the 2026–27 financial year uses the resident tax-free threshold of $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. For a dentist earning the NMW of $52,274.72, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $5,717, leaving a take-home pay of about $46,558 per year. For the average full-time earner at $108,352, tax would be approximately $24,467, leaving $83,885.

Remember that super is paid on top and does not reduce your take-home pay. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) on our site.

## Casual Loading and Award-Free Employees

If you are a casual dentist, you are entitled to the 25% casual loading on the NMW. This means your hourly rate is $33.05, and your annual gross would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80. The loading is intended to cover entitlements like annual leave and sick leave that casuals do not receive.

It is important never to include the casual loading in the base rate you enter into a calculator. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to correctly apply the loading.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember that the calculator assumes 38 hours per week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay.

For award-covered employees, pay rates are set by the relevant award. Dentists are not covered by any award, but if you work in a public hospital or under a specific enterprise agreement, different rules may apply. Check your employment contract or consult the [pay guides](/blog) for more information.

## Summary

A dentist salary Australia can range from the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour to well over $50 per hour for experienced practitioners. The key is to understand your employment status: award-free employees get the NMW, while those under enterprise agreements or self-employed may earn much more. Use the formula hourly × hours per week × 52 to convert to annual, and remember that super is paid on top. For a quick estimate, try our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page or the hourly conversion tool.
